subject: FinCo - migration compatibility & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinCo - migration compatibility & next tests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we have the plan captured:

Summary from today
- FinCo is evaluating migration from the Hyperscaler-managed endpoints to a vendor-managed inference platform for better cost predictability and VPC controls.
- Key requirements: OpenAI-compatible API surface, streaming support, prompt/response parity, token accounting, and SOC2 evidence for audit.
- Must validate that current prompt prompts/contexts produce identical outputs (or within tolerances) and that SDK swap is minimal for the engineering team.

Proposed next tests (what we will run)
1) OpenAI API compatibility smoke tests (GET/POST models, streaming, function-calling stubs) — target: parity for 95% of existing prompt space.
2) Prompt diff suite: sample ~200 production prompts across generation, chat, and reranking. Compare outputs (top-k, logprobs where available) and produce diff report.
3) Latency/cost test: 1k concurrent short-chat requests + 100 long-seq requests to compare p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost vs Hyperscaler.
4) SDK swap proof-of-concept: small repo showing 3-line changes using our OpenAI-compat SDK shim.
5) Security/compliance checklist: KMS expectations, VPC peering, audit log retention — we’ll map your SOC2 controls to our evidence.

Deliverables & owners
- Redwood: test plan, scripts, sample outputs, Hyperscaler comparison table (Marissa) — attached.
- Redwood SE: run compatibility tests and triage diffs (Neha).
- FinCo: provide production prompt set (anonymized) and example payloads (Sarah/Tom).

Timing
- Aim to kick off the POC week of June 1. Initial compatibility report by June 9.

Attachments: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.pdf, finco-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-table.csv

Next steps
- Sarah: confirm you can share an anonymized prompt corpus and a contact on infra to approve the VPC peering test.
- Neha: can you confirm availability to run the tests the week of June 1?

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear plan. A couple of clarifying Qs before we share the prompt corpus:
1) Streaming parity: does Redwood support chunked streaming with the same event framing we use today (data: {delta})? Any differences we should expect in framing or partial tokens?
2) Function calling / structured output: we rely on deterministic function-calls for several workflows. How do you handle ambiguous cases where multiple functions match?
3) Cost calc: your per-token accounting — can you provide a sample calculation using our current 50M tokens/month baseline?

We can provide anonymized prompts and a staging API key for the first pass. Tom will coordinate on infra.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director of ML Engineering | FinCo

Subject: Fwd: FinCo - migration compatibility & next tests

Forwarding Sarah's note — I can take the compatibility runs. Quick replies inline:

1) Streaming framing: We use the same chunked-event framing and support the common SSE-style data: lines. There are minor differences in how partial tokens are emitted (our runtime consolidates merged deltas for certain tokenizers), but we include a streaming compatibility mode that reproduces per-token partial deltas for strict parity.

2) Function calling: Our runtime exposes the same function-call resolution order, but we include a confidence threshold that you can tune. When multiple functions match equally, we return the top candidate and log alternative matches in the structured metadata; we can also configure deterministic tie-breaking to match your current behavior.

3) Cost calc: Attached is a sample calc for 50M tokens/month comparing Hyperscaler list pricing vs Redwood with reserved capacity and caching assumptions. Short version: expected per-token cost reduction of ~22% with a 3-month commitment and prefix caching.

I'll run the prompt-diff harness against your anonymized corpus once Sarah shares it. I have availability June 1–4 for the initial runs.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Sarah — perfect. Quick follow-up notes and what we'll deliver in the kickoff:

- Streaming: Neha will enable the strict streaming compatibility mode for the POC to mirror your current framing. Expect identical "data:" events barring tokenizer micro-diffs; we'll call those out in the report.
- Function calling: we'll set deterministic tie-breaking to match your existing resolver. If you can send two examples where ambiguity occurred, we will include them in the test set.
- Cost sample: attaching the 50M-token calc and the Hyperscaler comparison table. See the assumptions tab in finco-test-plan.xlsx for caching and batching assumptions.

Logistics for the week of June 1:
- Tue, Jun 1 10:00 PT — kickoff call (30m) to review the corpus and infra access (invite to follow).
- Jun 2–4 — Neha runs tests, triages diffs.
- Fri, Jun 5 — preliminary findings email.
- Tue, Jun 9 — detailed report and next-step recommendations.

If that schedule looks good, can you confirm staging key and infra contact (Tom) by EOD Monday?

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
Marissa
